findings.text: follow-on: the pin asserts reset_to_status receives the prefix list from the CLI, which closes the gap the plan named, but it stops at the forwarding boundary — it does not assert that the rendered prefix reaches the reset's own WHERE clause, so a regression inside reset_to_status itself (rather than at the call site) would still pass this test; that rendering is pinned separately in tests/discovery/test_reset.py, so the coverage is split rather than lost.

follow-on: the reviewed run's single gate log header records revision ecf996bf (its base) although the arm collected 91 tests (the head set, the base arm being 90), and the manifest records no baseline_suite/after_suite, so neither the header nor a named arm field lets a later reader tell the head arm from the base; naming the head revision in the header and recording the two arms would remove the ambiguity.

justifications.durability: the pin is the durability mechanism the plan wanted — the prior code CLI test runs --scan-only and never reached the reset branch, so dropping path_prefixes from code.py:200 would have widened --reset-to to every JT-60SA code file with a green suite; the new test makes that edit fail (independently shown against my own mutant). It guards the CLI-to-reset forwarding only, leaving the reset's own rendering pinned where it already is in tests/discovery/test_reset.py.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced the reviewed head myself — env -C <reviewed-worktree> python -m pytest tests/discovery/test_code_pipeline.py prints 91 passed, EXIT=0 (head.log), module.__file__ resolving to the reviewed tree; I built an independent mutant (the worktree package copied to $TMPDIR with code.py:200 reduced to reset_to_status(spec, facility)) and the same test fails with AssertionError: assert None == ['/analysis/src/SAeqread'] (negctl.log, EXIT=1, module.__file__ = the mutant); the baseline arm (a copy of the head test file without the new test) is 90 passed, EXIT=0 (base.log). The reviewed run's own negative_control.log (1 failed, EXIT=1) agrees. The deduction that the reviewed manifest carries no baseline_suite/after_suite is why the added-failure count is taken from the run's single gate log against this review's own baseline.
justifications.fit: the test name test_code_cli_reset_receives_path_prefixes and the docstring describe the mechanism (the reset branch is reached and the prefix list threads through) with no plan label, version or author attribution; the fragment element ids (code-reset-scope-pin-record, code-reset-scope-pin-landing) open with the node id, matching the sibling fragments.

justifications.reuse: the test joins the existing TestPathPrefixScan class and reuses the established CliRunner/monkeypatch-and-MagicMock idiom already in test_code_pipeline.py (test_code_cli_forwards_path_prefixes), adding no new fixtures, helpers or facilities.
